prompt_text: Who is the best marketing agency in Maryland?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no one objectively “best” marketing agency for every situation — the right agency depends on your business, goals, budget, industry, and preferred working style. I can help you find the best fit. Quick questions to narrow it down:

- What are your primary goals? (brand awareness, lead generation, e‑commerce sales, content, PR, events, SEO, paid media, etc.)
- What industry are you in?
- Do you prefer a local agency (Maryland) or are remote teams OK?
- What’s your approximate monthly or project budget?
- Do you want a full‑service firm or a specialist (SEO, performance marketing, creative, B2B, etc.)?
- Timeline — ongoing retainer vs one-off project/campaign?
- Any must-haves (e.g., marketing automation, HubSpot/Marketo experience, bilingual content)?

How I can help next
- If you answer the questions above I will research and shortlist 3–5 Maryland (or regional) agencies that match your needs, with pros/cons and likely pricing ranges.
- Or I can give a short RFP and evaluation rubric you can use to compare agencies yourself.

Quick guidance on choosing the “best” agency
- Relevant experience: case studies in your industry and measurable results.
- Services & capabilities: do they cover everything you need or work well with partners?
- Culture/communication: responsiveness, reporting cadence, named team members.
- Measurement: clear KPIs and transparent reporting dashboards.
- References: speak to 2–3 current/former clients.
- Tech stack: experience with your platforms (CMS, CRM, ad accounts, analytics).
- Budget fit: avoid both underpriced (inexperienced) and overpriced (overhead) mismatches.

Useful resources to find reputable agencies
- Clutch.co, UpCity, G2 — searchable by location and service
- Local business publications (e.g., Baltimore Business Journal) and trade awards
- LinkedIn and referrals from peers in your industry

Sample short RFP questions (useful when contacting agencies)
1. Brief description of your firm and core services.
2. Case study of a similar client and measurable outcomes.
3. Proposed scope and activities for our goals.
4. Team members who would work on our account and their experience.
5. Estimated timeline and key milestones.
6. Pricing model (retainer, project, hourly) and estimated cost range.
7. KPIs and reporting frequency/tools.
8. References (2–3 clients).
9. Contract terms / minimum commitment.
10. Examples of creative or media work.

If you want, tell me your goals, industry, and budget and I’ll shortlist a few Maryland agencies and give a recommended next step. Which option do you prefer?
